nodes.name: Upsert Contact
nodes.notes: Upserts on the tenant_id+email unique constraint from Phase 5. Deliberately no lead scoring/escalation here -- this just makes sure an email from a new sender gets a contact row, same as chat does via capture_lead, so email leads don't fall outside the pipeline. TODO: confirm 'contacts' table has no other NOT NULL columns beyond tenant_id/email that would make a bare insert fail (e.g. a required 'source' or 'name' column) -- add them to the insert if so.

parameters.query:
-- Replaces the current query in "Get or Create Conversation (Email)".
-- Old version only returned a row on first creation -- returned nothing if
-- the conversation already existed, which is fine when nothing downstream
-- needs the ID, but message-logging needs a reliable ID every time.
with existing as (
  select id from conversations
  where tenant_id = $1 and contact_id = $2 and channel = 'email'
  limit 1
),
inserted as (
  insert into conversations (tenant_id, contact_id, channel)
  select $1, $2, 'email'
  where not exists (select 1 from existing)
  returning id
)
select id from existing
union all
select id from inserted;

nodes.name: Get or Create Conversation (Email)
nodes.notes: TODO: this INSERT...WHERE NOT EXISTS returns nothing on the 'already exists' path (a Postgres quirk) -- you'll need a follow-up SELECT (or a CTE combining both) to reliably get the conversation_id either way. Also confirm 'conversations' table actually has a 'channel' column -- if it doesn't, this needs a small migration too, and email threads should probably map many gmail_thread_ids to one ongoing conversation per contact rather than one-per-thread; adjust the matching logic if so.

parameters.query:
-- 0039: the agency whose Elliot address (<slug>@in.getelliot.eu) or own address
-- is among the recipients. Always one row (empty if none), so an unknown
-- address is logged.
select m.* from (select 1) x
left join lateral email_inbound_tenant($1::text[]) m on true;
